concepts.title: Satyajit's Fall from the Summit
concepts.definition: Bhabani Bhattacharya's Satyajit Datta was a self-made financial wizard -- a village boy who rose to be a director of a nationalised bank, his portrait in newspapers, a garlanded hero. Then the bank crashes overnight in a scandal, his colleagues are arrested, and Satyajit, the honest one, resigns in disgrace and takes a slow train home.
concepts.key_idea: Glory has a twilight -- the honest man still rides the downfall his institution's scandal produces.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww107.txt rise and fall sections (satyajit datta director of the bank, rise from village, bank crash scandal, resignation, train journey home)

solution_steps.explain: From a village boy to director of the bank, Satyajit had known fame, portraits and garlands.
A financial scandal topples the bank; though personally honest, Satyajit loses his position overnight.
He boards a crowded train in ordinary clothes -- a fallen grandee returning to his roots.

concepts.title: The Village Wedding Invitation
concepts.definition: On the train and at his village home, Satyajit is drawn into old bonds: distant relatives invite him to a family wedding, and the collector of his childhood -- the memory of his mother, the pond, the school -- floods back. Invited to bless the bride, he is asked to give money he can barely afford, straddling old obligation and new poverty.
concepts.key_idea: Poverty meets obligation -- the fallen hero must still play the rich man at the village wedding.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww107.txt wedding sections (invitation to the wedding, relatives' expectations, gift money dilemma, memories of mother and school)
question_patterns: why is satyajit invited to the wedding in the village
in class 11 glory at twilight: what dilemma does the wedding gift create for satyajit

solution_steps.explain: The relatives expect the famous financier to arrive with the grandeur of his former position.
His purse emptied by the crash, Satyajit still cannot refuse a village girl's wedding or his mother's memory.
He gives what he honestly can -- dignity over display, love over reputation.

concepts.title: Sajjan's Offer and the Price of Integrity
concepts.definition: His nephew Sajjan, now prosperous through less honest means, offers Satyajit a partnership and easy recovery of status -- asking only that he lend his sterling name to dubious business. Satyajit refuses: he will return to his village and teach, keeping his integrity when his fortune is gone.
concepts.key_idea: Name for sale or name kept whole -- the fallen financier refuses to mortgage his one remaining asset.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww107.txt sajan sections (sajjan's business offer, lending the name, refusal, decision to return to teaching and village)

solution_steps.explain: Sajjan dangles partnership, money and restored glory in exchange for the use of Satyajit's unblemished name.
Satyajit sees that his name is all he has left -- lending it to shady venture would finish even that.
He returns to his village roots and teaching, choosing integrity over twilight glory regained.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The wedding gift dilemma: explain why Satyajit cannot refuse the invitation despite his poverty.

solution_template.explain: Family bonds, his late mother's ties, and the village's memory of his greatness all press him to attend.
Attending means giving generously -- from a purse the bank crash has emptied.
He attends with honest affection rather than performative wealth -- the story's definition of real glory.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Sajjan calls Satyajit's refusal foolish pride. Present Satyajit's defence.

solution_template.explain: Refusing wealth and recovery does look like pride to a man like Sajjan.
The offer demands his name over dishonest business -- the one thing the crash left untouched.
It is not pride but principle: a name spent on wrong can never buy back honour.
